name: Amen break
what: A four-bar drum solo, about six seconds long.
paid: Neither Coleman nor copyright owner Richard Spencer received royalties; a 2015 fundraiser gave Spencer a goodwill payment.

name: Funky Drummer
what: An eight-bar drum solo of about 20 seconds.
used_by: Public Enemy, LL Cool J, George Michael, Ed Sheeran
paid: Stubblefield was not credited as a writer and got little or no royalties.

name: Think break
what: The drum loop, the tambourine and the shouted vocal stab.
used_by: Rob Base and DJ E-Z Rock, Cookie Crew, Kanye West, Snoop Dogg

name: Apache
player: King Errisson on percussion; kit drummer disputed (Jim Gordon or Kat Hendrikse)
what: The long drum and bongo break.
used_by: Sugarhill Gang, Grandmaster Flash, Goldie, Nas

name: Impeach the President
what: The opening bar of drums.
used_by: MC Shan, Audio Two, The Notorious B.I.G., Nas
paid: Writer-producer Roy C had earned no royalties from sample use as of 2018.

name: Synthetic Substitution
what: The kick-heavy opening groove.
used_by: Public Enemy, Ultramagnetic MCs, The Pharcyde, Wu-Tang Clan

name: Levee break
what: The opening drums, recorded in a stairwell at Headley Grange.
used_by: Beastie Boys, Dr. Dre, Eminem, Björk
paid: Jimmy Page never took legal action over the Beastie Boys' use.

name: It's a New Day
what: The drums.

name: The Big Beat
what: The opening drums.
used_by: Run-DMC, Jay-Z, Dizzee Rascal, Alicia Keys

name: Mardi Gras
artist: Bob James - "Take Me to the Mardi Gras"
what: The opening drums and bell pattern.

name: Nautilus
what: The bassline and the sonar-like synth.
used_by: Ultramagnetic MC's, Run-DMC, Slick Rick, A Tribe Called Quest

name: UFO
what: The siren-like guitar figure at the top.
used_by: Big Daddy Kane, Public Enemy, The Notorious B.I.G., J Dilla
paid: ESG went about 20 years without compensation; royalties began after a 2000 compilation.

name: Ashley's Roachclip
what: The break at about 3:36.
used_by: Eric B. and Rakim, PM Dawn, Milli Vanilli, EMF

name: Papa Was Too
what: Open drums with a tambourine on beat two.
used_by: EPMD, Wu-Tang Clan, Common, Dr. Dre

name: Funky President
what: The drums.

name: The "fresh" scratch
player: Voice disputed: Roger Trilling or Fab 5 Freddy
what: A tone and a vocoder line ending on the word "fresh", at the end of the B-side.
used_by: Herbie Hancock, Eric B. and Rakim, Beastie Boys, Macklemore
paid: Writer Bernard Zekri, Roger Trilling and Beside say they were not paid.

name: Trans-Europe Express / Numbers
what: The melody of one and the beat of the other, replayed, not sampled, on "Planet Rock".
used_by: Afrika Bambaataa and the Soulsonic Force, Cybotron
paid: By the account of those involved, Tommy Boy agreed to pay Kraftwerk $1 per record sold.

name: Volt Mix
artist: DJ Battery Brain - "8 Volt Mix" (B-side "808 Beatapella Mix")
what: A Roland TR-808 beat that anchored 1990s funk carioca.

name: Sleng Teng
player: Preset written by Okuda Hiroko; played by Noel Davey
what: The "rock" rhythm preset of the Casio MT-40.
paid: Casio chose not to sue and asks for a credit line and no fee.

name: Thoda Resham Lagta Hai
artist: Lata Mangeshkar - "Thoda Resham Lagta Hai" (film Jyoti)
what: The vocal recording, used on "Addictive".

name: More Spell on You
what: The lead sample of "One More Time".
paid: Johns had received nothing as of May 2021; Daft Punk's label says it pays the track's owner.
